editorial_thesis: Persistent agents are moving into operating workflows, while security controls and context portability decide whether they can be trusted.

topic_groups.title: Persistent agents move from prompt to operating layer
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Fresh practical signal and a coverage gap; avoids yesterday’s runtime-control, privacy, and architecture lanes.

sources.title: Dots: an always-on project steward
sources.why_selected: The unit of automation becomes an owned workstream with memory and review.
sources.usefulness: Prototype a bounded project steward that maintains a decision log and returns reviewable artifacts.

sources.title: GPT-6.1 Sol: lower-cost long-horizon work
sources.why_selected: Cheap context reuse changes the economics of agents that revisit project state.
sources.usefulness: Benchmark Buildn tasks by quality, retries, latency, and cost.

sources.title: DevDay: cloud agents, code review, private intelligence
sources.why_selected: The toolchain is converging around remote execution plus review surfaces.
sources.usefulness: Map Buildn artifacts to isolated workspaces, human review, and immutable links.

sources.title: GPT-6.1 Sol arrives inside GitHub Copilot
sources.why_selected: Model choice is now close to the repository and workflow where adoption happens.

topic_groups.title: Agent security is becoming an operating plane
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Fresh practical signal and a coverage gap; avoids yesterday’s runtime-control, privacy, and architecture lanes.

sources.title: Google Cloud’s partner security-agent layer
sources.why_selected: Security work is packaged as orchestrable action across existing systems.
sources.usefulness: Build discover → assess → propose → approve → contain → record-evidence adapters.

sources.title: ISACA’s 11-category agent security baseline
sources.why_selected: It gives clients a common vocabulary for threat-modeling the full workflow.
sources.usefulness: Turn categories into Buildn intake and release gates.

sources.title: Agent Gateway + Registry as the control seam
sources.why_selected: A central seam can enforce identity, routing, policy, and telemetry.
sources.usefulness: Represent integrations as registered capabilities with scopes, owners, health, and evidence contracts.

sources.title: Security posture becomes an integration surface
sources.why_selected: Clients will expect agent security to connect to existing controls.
sources.usefulness: Package a readiness sprint around inventory, permissions, tests, and reversible response.

topic_groups.title: The overlooked leverage is durable context and migration hygiene
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Fresh practical signal and a coverage gap; avoids yesterday’s runtime-control, privacy, and architecture lanes.

sources.title: Gemini API change windows make migration visible
sources.why_selected: Agent systems need ordinary dependency hygiene: pins, contract tests, and deprecation calendars.
sources.usefulness: Add provider-change monitoring to every integration.

sources.title: Knowledge management is an AI readiness constraint
sources.why_selected: Agent quality is bounded by freshness, ownership, and reuse of knowledge.
sources.usefulness: Sell a knowledge map and maintenance loop before promising an enterprise agent.

sources.title: Physical AI needs digital-twin-first workflows
sources.why_selected: Simulation reduces the cost of experimenting with real-world agents.
sources.usefulness: Use plan → simulate → verify → deploy for high-cost automation.

sources.title: Voice becomes an API primitive
sources.why_selected: Voice can remove friction from field intake when identity and audit are explicit.
sources.usefulness: Prototype voice intake that creates a structured task and asks for confirmation.
